compositionRules.reason: The page title establishes the primary reading level.
Task pages reserve room for data and controls.
A section groups related content rather than promoting each child.
Section titles remain subordinate to a task, commerce or reading page title.
Nested surfaces use the existing smaller inset relation S05.
A feature card explains one concept; its title and copy form one group.
Product identity and price take precedence over a promotional heading.
Author and metadata identify reading content; preserve its editorial hierarchy.
Supporting information does not compete with task page headings.
Give values and mixed-script glyphs sufficient room before reducing their font; decoration is secondary.
Fields form a group; label/help proximity stays smaller than field separation.
Settings use the same field grammar as forms, within a task context.
Repeated data rows follow density rather than a fixed cell padding.
List items remain related within their enclosing component.
Hero copy is one group; the action is the next group. Media fits its content box instead of viewport-based negative bleed.
Two columns require room in the containing region, independently of viewport width.
The existing orphan-free flow owns column selection; content supplies its minimum cell width.
A primary form uses the existing larger inset; a secondary form retains the component inset.
